newsitem.title: MEXICO: INTERVIEW - Mexico's Bancomext looks at another bond.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Mexico's Bancomext looks at another bond.

text.p: Mexican development bank Banco Nacional de Comercio Exterior (Bancomext) is considering placing a five- to 10-year bond worth between $250 to $300 million this month, a bank official said on Wednesday.

The bond would be in U.S. dollars and would mark the first bond issue by the bank since May last year, said Julio Mendez Rubio, the bank's assistant director general for finances said in an interview.

"We are in the process of deciding on the next one, and with all probability we will be going this month, in June," Mendez said. "It will certainly be in dollars, between $250 million and $300 million."

"It could be five or 10 years, but I would repeat that it is not a done decision. We are still considering the alternatives since we think that the markets at this time are favorable for a placement," he said.
Bancomext is looking for a spread similar to two recent issues by other quasi-sovereign Mexican issuers.

State-owned oil company Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) placed a 10-year $250 million bond in late May at 223 basis points over U.S. Treasuries. A week earlier development bank Nacional Financiera (Nafin) placed a three-year $150 million Eurobond at 140 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.
"We have very good conditions right now in respect to spreads," Mendez said.
The development bank is considering placing bonds worth between $500 million and $1.0 billion during the entire year, with much depending on demand for credit and economic conditions.
"What we have noticed is that the demand for credit is growing, especially for investments for new projects, and for expanding existing projects," he said.

"Because of this we are thinking that for the whole year the bank could place bonds worth between $500 million and $1.0 billion," Mendez said. The markets and currencies for those bond issues could vary.

"With respect to the market that we place an issue in, it depends a lot on where we can get the best conditions. It could be in German marks, or in the yen market or in the Yankee market or in Eurobonds in pounds sterling.

"It depends on where we can get the best conditions," he said. Another factor in its decisions is that Bancomext swaps out issues into U.S. dollars, since its credits to exporters are also in U.S. dollars.

The last time Bancomext went to the capital markets was in May last year, when it placed a 10-year $250 million bond in Europe and the United States. That bond had a spread of 470 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.
In March last year, it placed a 300 million mark three-year floating-rate note, at 325 basis points over three-month LIBOR.
To finance longer-term projects Bancomext places debt issues with a mimimum of a five year term.
But the bank also has an active short-term borrowing program with commercial banks and uses commercial paper to help foster exports.
The company renewed its $300 million commercial paper program in the U.S. at the end of last year for another year.
Mendez said the development bank will likely renew that commercial paper program again at the end of this year.
Bancomext is the second largest development bank after Nafin and promotes and finances foreign trade.
Standard & Poor's has a double BB rating on Bancomext, with a stable outlook, in line with the sovereign ceiling.
